survivingClaim: Precise obstruction stands; no statement about zeros of zeta; headline unchanged. Confirmed: the complete band-u positivity device is the quadratic form of T_Z on L^2 of an interval of length u (classical Weil/Yoshida frame, C(theta) tests modulated indicators only); a cluster of n off-line pairs has exactly n negative directions; one pair against a tight on-line background alpha is invisible exactly up to sinh(ub)/(ub) = 1 + (alpha+2M)/u; in the lattice model above u = log(t/2pi) an exact device (M = 0) excludes every finite cluster, and with tolerance M one pair passes below the root of u(sinh(ub)/(ub)-1) = 2M (about sqrt(12M) u^(-3/2)) and is excluded above the root of (sin^2+sinh^2) mu(b, u-Lg) = 2M (two-sided, not an asymptotic equality); infinite rows of spacing <= 2pi/u pass with any offset; one cluster satisfies u b_max <= 5.85 n + logs relative to Turan's second main theorem; tapered half-Nyquist rows pass with slope about 0.44 per pair (measured, reproduced). The truncated Euler product identity holds for every completely multiplicative chain and no step uses it. Not established: the density form of W4, the sequence form of W5, and the DH and zeta(s+a)zeta(s-a) control rows as written (the latter passes for theta' <= 1 in the lattice model).
obstruction: A band-limited positivity device has a density reach, not a zero-free region. lesson: The reach of a band-limited positivity device is a density condition, not a zero-free region: off-line pairs hide only at local density of order u/2pi, and two bands are structural (P = sqrt(t/2pi) for count-preserving configurations, P = t/2pi for exactness). Multiplicativity is present exactly at every band (truncated Euler product in the truncated-shift algebra) for every multiplicative chain, so the missing input is a one-sided operator bound tied to the functional-equation reserve, not the factorisation. Above the Nyquist band only M = 0 has full power, and that is the target itself in a window.
